Annual resizing and far-only routing do not constitute a globally optimal persistent infrastructure solution.

Authors acknowledge single well per pipeline/reservoir, need for BHP fracture control, neglected hydrostatic head, absent intermediate boosters and fixed hub/spoke topology. Future booster balance and branch networks inspected. No multiwell, booster, branching or pressure-safe alternative is actually reproduced. Average pressure passing is a weaker condition than BHP passing whenever injection pressure increment is positive, even for a highly injective reservoir.

Screening value and the need to consider pressure/injectivity early are methodological conclusions. The authors describe an exploratory short-duration project and call for detailed reservoir/flow validation. No quantitative predictive uncertainty, independent case validation, global-optimum proof, current site access or lifecycle-retention result established.

equations.assessment: Positive RHS is naturally a loss magnitude; signed downstream pressure gradient requires a convention. Constant/local fluid properties and homogeneous single-phase flow are assumptions. Bathymetry/thermal/phase behavior are not represented by this expression.

Relative roughness and Reynolds number are dimensionless. Explicit turbulent approximation; numerical validity range, pipe roughness and actual caseRe not provided. No laminar/transition or mixed-phase extension inferred.

equations.expression: P_r^(t+1)/z(P_r^(t+1)) = P_r^t/z(P_r^t) + Delta_m_t R T/(M V_p)
equations.assessment: From n=PV/(zRT) under fixedT,Vp and suitable gas composition. IncrementDelta_m is mass, not mass rate; requires time conversion. z(P) makes pressure update implicit and not generally linear inP. Residual methane/brine/rock/aquifer states,EOS and solve policy missing.

Average-pressure bound is weaker than local BHP bound forpositive flow. No universal conservatism or full storage-integrity guarantee. End-of-step headroom, clipping/rescaling and mass conservation need code.

equations.expression: P_bh^2 = P_r^2 + mdot mu z R T/(M k h) [ln(r_e/r_w) - 0.75]
equations.units: Pa2 in SI; absolute pressure required by gas density law
equations.assessment: Printed relation has no explicitpi. Independent axisymmetric SI integration has1/pi for the same shape term under stated assumptions. Original Dake geometry/unit convention and author code unverified. Constantmu/z/T, single-gas compressibility and pseudo-steady shape are not a real-fluid dense-phase derivation; skin is explicitly omitted.

No hydrostatic contribution in implemented model despite narrative. Capture-pressure reference/state and controls missing. Nonnegative power/pressure-rise treatment when supplied pressure exceeds demand is not specified; no negative-cost recovery credit inferred.

Dimensionally consistent constant-density pumping approximation. Not a complete gas-compression enthalpy/thermal integral from near-atmospheric capture. Fluid state, efficiency, stages,heat rejection and hydrostatic effects missing.

equations.units: currency/year only with compatible power/hour/tariff units

equations.assessment: D andL conventions, dimensional cost coefficient,currency year and omitted base factor unresolved. A dimensionless multiplier1.2 alone cannot assign money. m-versus-km input changes raw output1000fold; no convention silently selected.

Bounds,annualisation,solver andflow used in each minimisation absent. Minimum annual cost is not automatically marginalcurrency/mass; derivative/normalisation needed. Reoptimisation does not create a persistent fixed-size pipeline.

equations.units: cost if unitcost andtime/rate conventions agree

qmax values andremaining pressure headroom dependence missing. Start-of-year availability alone can overshoot next-state limit; code may add controls, but they are unverified.

Acknowledged future/local safety constraint, not enforced in reported case. P_bh>P_r implies averagebound alone cannot logically guarantee it, even ifgradient is small.

equations.expression: Analyst: mdot = 2 pi r h k rho/mu * |dp/dr|; rho=M p/(zRT); integrate p dp to obtain Delta(P^2)=mdot mu zRT/(pi Mkh) * shape
equations.units: Pa2 under constant mu/z/T,axisymmetric gas assumptions
equations.assessment: Independent geometry derivation, not an author equation or verified Dake passage. Hold shape=ln(re/rw)−.75 only for coefficient comparison; no claim of rigorous dense-phase validation or repair of unpublished code.

variables: P, x, L and D: pressure, axial coordinate, length and internal diameter. SI uses Pa and m; plots use bar, m and km. Pressure basis/datum is unreported. Eq1 has a positive pressure-loss RHS; a signed-gradient convention is needed.

Mass flow mdot [kg/s], velocity [m/s], density [kg/m3], area [m2], Darcy friction factor/Reynolds number [dimensionless], viscosity [Pa.s], roughness [m]. Actual fluid states, composition, property backend and software releases are missing.

P_r, P_bh, P_frac, P_cap, Delta_P_pipe and Delta_P_tot distinguish average reservoir pressure, flowing BHP, fracture pressure, capture pressure, pipe loss and total rise. P/z and pressure-squared gas laws need absolute pressure; the bar plot label does not resolve the basis.

z(P), universal R [J/mol/K], reservoir T [K], molar mass M [kg/mol], pore volume V_p [m3] and increment Delta_m [kg]. Rate must be integrated over time. Fixed T/volume and suitable composition are assumptions; residual methane, brine, rock and aquifer behavior are not fully described.

Permeability k [m2], thickness h [m] and dimensionless radius ratio r_e/r_w. Any mD or mPa.s conversion must be explicit. Eq5 omits skin and assumes a gas-flow shape term. The later booster index k means a segment, not permeability.

W is power; eta is efficiency; C_el is electricity tariff; C_OPEX and C_CAPEX are annual operating/capital costs; k_capex is a coefficient/multiplier. Numerical power/tariff/currency/length units, year and annualisation/discount basis are not supplied.

q_i,t, Q_t and q_i,max: allocation rate, demand rate and bounds. Mtpa is a rate, despite some volume wording. Twenty project years,8760-hour annualisation, the stated five-year ramp and Figure4 year0–19 must be distinguished. No exact native demand or annual output array is retained.

c_i(P_r^t) is asserted as marginal/unit cost without a derivation. Annual total cost from Eq10 needs differentiation or normalisation before it can be a cost per mass. Flow-dependent diameter optimisation does not automatically yield a globally fixed linear coefficient.

Reservoir index i and annual time t differ from the segment index k. Start/end pressure indexing, rate caps and remaining pressure headroom are unprovided. Binary activation and PSO settings are omitted; no global MILP/PSO is reproduced.

One well is assigned per reservoir/pipeline. Four modified anonymous routes are Near10km, Mid1/Mid2 each100km and Far300km. They do not establish named operational storage or access. Multiwell sharing and brine management are not implemented.

Background ranges include100–200bar delivery,600–900kg/m3 density,16–24inch pipes,0.1bar/km losses and20–30°C/4°C seabed. These are not matched cases or uncertainty distributions. Pure critical31.1°C/73.8bar and generic−20°C cooling discussion are not universal mixture/material limits.

Dense phase is assumed, but complete EOS/composition/temperature and phase/solid/hydrate controls are absent. Skin and hydrostatic head are omitted from the implemented case, despite their discussion in the value-chain narrative.
Quoted maximum diameter0.50→0.55m is distinct from each annually changing curve. Installed size, commercial bounds, material/thickness/pressure rating and upgrade/cost rules are unprovided.

USD230/148 million are quoted comparison values. Figure6 endpoint approximately275–290 million is a visual estimate range, not native or corrected data. No verified saving, NPV, observed cost or full inventory is adopted.

All analyst SI/constraint examples are separate from author inputs. Approximate plot readings provide no calibrated annual maximum service, statistical uncertainty, retention probability or lifecycle-GHG factor.

claims.claim: MILP and nature-inspired comparison provide optimal safe selection
claims.assessment: The body presents annual economic dispatch and explicitly omits full MILP/PSO. No global formulation, code, optimality gap, runtime or stochastic comparison is supplied. Average-pressure passing with BHP exceedance is not proof of safe injection or global optimality.

claims.claim: Cited studies support physics-based reservoir dynamics in MILP
claims.assessment: Bertoni primary passages support POD–TPWL coupling and an explicit BHP constraint; their accuracy does not transfer here. The inspected d’Amore annual-cost network formulation does not establish the joint pressure-dynamic attribution. Other originals remain unverified.

claims.claim: Dense-phase hydraulics give reliable screening predictions
claims.assessment: Exact source validation/conditions are unverified. Generic critical pressure and property ranges cannot replace composition-aware phase and thermal checks. The narrative includes mechanisms omitted from the implemented model.

claims.claim: P/z and average pressure conservatively ensure integrity
claims.assessment: Uniform gas-tank behavior is a screening approximation, not shown universally conservative. Positive injection gradients make the BHP constraint stricter. The authors explicitly allow fracture-limit exceedance and acknowledge the risk; allocations are not demonstrated safe annual service.

claims.claim: Physics/cost model supplies marginal costs and allocations
claims.assessment: Native data, PVT, units, marginal-cost derivation, rate caps, pressure headroom and solver are missing. Eq5 geometry, Eq8 power/tariff basis and Eq9 cost normalisation require clarification. No full case or unpublished-code defect is established.

claims.claim: Demand reaches10Mtpa during the first five years
claims.assessment: Figure4 reaches that level around year10 after smaller steps. Native demand and time indexing are missing. Preserve both assertions; no exact annual total is invented or integrated from pixels.

claims.claim: Far has superior injectivity; Mid2 has the elevated BHP
claims.assessment: The highest curve is labelled Mid1; orange Mid2 is lower but above the dashed limit. Do not swap identities. Comparative injectivity cannot be quantified without native kh, geometry, fluid and rate data.

claims.claim: First-use CAPEX and annual D choices give optimal infrastructure
claims.assessment: Persistent fixed sizes and upgrade constraints/costs are missing. Annual resizing does not create physical pipe capacity for free. Dispatch and once-only accounting need reconciliation with global investment planning.

The quoted82million/35.65% arithmetic is not a verified saving. Figure6 baseline is visibly above250, roughly275–290. Native arrays, safety, fixed assets, equivalent service and complete cost boundaries remain unresolved; no corrected author value is imposed.

claims.claim: Longer routing to a good reservoir can beat nearby tight storage
claims.assessment: A useful hypothesis illustrated by unverified screening cases; not a universal routing rule or field calibration. It needs BHP-safe, multiwell, hydrostatic, fixed-design and matched-inventory comparisons.

claims.claim: The framework supports net zero and permanent safe storage
claims.assessment: No complete capture/conditioning/utility/well/brine/asset/monitoring inventory, carbon mass balance or post-closure horizon is supplied. Policy context is not lifecycle mitigation or retention validation.
